title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continuing from the previous pages). Let \hat\Pi_{0,3} be the profinite fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,\infty}, a free profinite group on two generators l_0 and l_1 (with l_\infty also defined). Let \hat{\mathfrak S}^+_{0,3} be the extension of \mathfrak S_3 by \hat\Pi_{0,3}, i.e. the profinite fundamental group of the stack M_{0,3}/\mathfrak S_3.

The group \hat{\mathfrak S}^+_{0,3} has the presentation with generators \sigma_\infty, \rho and relations \sigma_\infty^2 = \rho^3 = 1. So it is the profinite completion of Z/2 * Z/3 = PSL_2(Z). In this picture \hat\Pi_{0,3} is the index-6 congruence subgroup \Gamma(2)/\pm1, and the quotient is \mathfrak S_3 = PSL_2(F_2).

Previous page. E^! = Aut(\hat{\mathfrak S}^+_{0,3} | identity on \mathfrak S_3) is a split extension by \hat\Pi_{0,3}. A splitting is the subgroup of automorphisms with u(\sigma_\infty) = \sigma_\infty and u(\rho) = g\rho, g \in \hat\Pi_{0,3} (formula 36).

This page, first part. Such an assignment defines an endomorphism exactly when the relations of the presentation are respected, i.e. when (38) (g\rho)^3 = 1, equivalently g\rho(g)\rho^2(g) = 1, where \rho(g) = \rho g \rho^{-1}. The margin adds the condition that \sigma_\infty and g\rho must generate the whole group with only the relations \sigma_\infty^2 = (g\rho)^3 = 1, so that the endomorphism is an automorphism. This is the cyclic ('hexagon') relation of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group, written as a cocycle condition for the order-3 automorphism \rho. The condition coming from \sigma_\infty is automatic here, since \sigma_\infty is fixed.

Main corollary. For u \in E^!, the following are equivalent:
- (a) u(l'_0) is conjugate in \hat{\mathfrak S}^+_{0,3} to l'_0^p for some p \in \hat Z^*. Here l'_0 = \varepsilon_0 is the 'half-twist', a square root of l_0 whose image in \mathfrak S_3 is the transposition \sigma_0, analogous to T = [[1,1],[0,1]] whose square lies in \Gamma(2).
- (b) u(l_0) is conjugate in \hat\Pi_{0,3} to l_0^p.
- (c) u_0 = u|\hat\Pi_{0,3} respects the inertia structure, i.e. maps each l_i to a conjugate of l_i^p.
In each case p is unique, and the p in (a) and (b) coincide.

Proof of (a) ⇒ (b) given on this page:
1. Square u(l'_0) = int(g_0)(l'_0^p) to get u(l_0) = int(g_0)(l_0^p).
2. u is the identity on \mathfrak S_3 and p is a unit, so the image of l'_0^p is \sigma_0. Hence the image of g_0 centralizes \sigma_0 in \mathfrak S_3, so it is 1 or \sigma_0.
3. If it is 1, (b) holds directly.
4. Otherwise write g_0 = h\sigma_0 with h \in \hat\Pi_{0,3}. Using \sigma_0(l_0) = int(a) l_0 with a \in \hat\Pi_{0,3}, conclude u(l_0) = int(ha)(l_0^p), with the same p.

The next page proves (b) ⇒ (c) by transporting with \rho, and (c) ⇒ (a) via uniqueness of the square root of l_0 among the relevant elements.

Purpose. This characterizes GT-type automorphisms (inertia-preserving, \mathfrak S_3-compatible) as automorphisms of \widehat{PSL_2(Z)}. It links the 'équation des lacets' to the modular group / M_{1,1} picture.
errors: No genuine mathematical error in the argument as written.
The phrase 'd'où b) avec c = p' is presumably a slip or misreading for 'with the same p'.

The next page calls \varepsilon_0 an 'involution' of square l_0; that is self-contradictory as written, since an element of finite order cannot square to an element of infinite order. Most likely it is a slip for 'the unique element of the given type (lifting \sigma_0) with square l_0'.
Uniqueness of p is asserted but not proved here; it follows from l_0 generating a procyclic subgroup that is its own normalizer up to conjugacy (standard for free profinite groups).

ideas.what: Presentation of the S_3-extension of \hat\pi_1(P^1-{0,1,\infty}) as \widehat{Z/2*Z/3} (profinite PSL_2(Z)) and of automorphisms fixing \sigma_\infty with \rho -> g\rho subject to (g\rho)^3=1
ideas.modern_name: GT-action on \widehat{PSL_2(Z)} / hexagon relation as 3-cocycle condition
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions the role of M_{0,4}, M_{1,1} and the \mathfrak S_3 symmetry; the explicit formula is not there as far as I know

ideas.what: Equivalence of conjugacy-to-power conditions on the half-twist in the extended group, on l_0 in \hat\Pi_{0,3}, and preservation of the full inertia structure
ideas.modern_name: inertia-preserving (cuspidal) automorphisms of the profinite free group / tripod

missed.claim: Grothendieck works directly with the 'modular' presentation \widehat{PSL_2(Z)} = <\sigma_\infty,\rho | \sigma_\infty^2=\rho^3=1>. In it, GT-type automorphisms are normalized by fixing \sigma_\infty, and the cyclic GT relation appears as the norm-type cocycle condition g\rho(g)\rho^2(g)=1. Inertia preservation for all three punctures is shown to follow from a single condition on the half-twist l'_0 in the extended group. This is an early (pre-Drinfeld) independent formulation; the content is essentially known today.
missed.quote: (38) (g\rho)^3=1 i.e. g\rho(g)\rho^2(g)=1 ... Cor. Main ... u(l'_0) conjugué dans \hat{\mathfrak S}^+_{0,3} à l_0'^p
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority: it documents Grothendieck's own GT-like definition via automorphisms of profinite PSL_2(Z), predating Drinfeld's GT. Mathematically it is close to known reformulations, so of limited novelty.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a careful working out of a GT-type normalization and an inertia criterion that are now standard (Drinfeld, Ihara, Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura, Hoshi–Mochizuki). Its interest is mainly historical, as Grothendieck's independent pre-Drinfeld formulation via profinite PSL_2(Z).
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'écrivant que u est un automorphisme (car le groupe ...' is likely, rather than unreadable gaps.
Line 2: '\hat\Pi^+_{0,3}' should be '\hat{\mathfrak S}^+_{0,3}' (the group presented by \sigma_\infty, \rho).
Margin: '\hat\pi_{0,3}' generated by \sigma_\infty and g\rho should be \hat{\mathfrak S}^+_{0,3}.
In a), '\varepsilon_0' written under l'_0 is a notation gloss (l'_0 = \varepsilon_0), not a subscript of the formula.
In c), '[?]' is likely 'respecte la structure d'inertie de \hat\Pi_{0,3}'.
Last line: 'd'où b) avec c = p' is probably 'd'où b) avec le même p'.
